reason: planning stopped before any code was written: the plan still needed revising in the last round (round 3 of 3). The plan is detailed and mostly grounded in real code. These all exist with the shapes the plan relies on: `drain_concurrent` (drain.rs:2194), `Drain::land` with its `landing` mutex (drain.rs:1322), `attempts` with its two-call landing retry (drain.rs:1368-1438), `Git::replay`, `Git::exit`, `Git::reset_keep` (athena-git lib.rs:773, 240, 704), `attrs::fingerprint` (attrs.rs:139), `landed_commit_for` (landing.rs:78) and `Athena::ask` (reading.rs:827). The parentless-commit pre-check matches the `Refused` text in `replay`. Blocking a rebase whose governed fingerprint changed (NeedsRecheck) is backed by `observe_merge`, which checks the merge against the verified fingerprint (pr.rs:372), and the plan raises that scope tension with the user openly. Two gaps remain. First, the plan claims behaviour is unchanged only for a fully serial drain. It ignores the existing `[parallel] max_concurrency` > 1 path (main.rs:1144-1158), where max_in_flight is still 1 but group jobs land one after another onto a main that has moved. Second, it leaves as an open question what the old job's records look like after `drop_landed`, and whether a later drain picks the old job up again as work. Reading the code can settle that, and the answer decides whether the conflict return creates duplicate work. Both should be settled before the build. Findings: major: The plan never covers `[parallel] max_concurrency` > 1, which ships today and runs with max_in_flight = 1. The queue may change how that path lands. (Approach / Risks ('At max_in_flight = 1 ... the serial drain is unchanged'); Demonstrations criterion 4); major: What happens to the old job after its landing commit is dropped is left open. Yet it decides whether the conflict return makes duplicate work, and reading the code can settle it. (Decision 4 (`send_back` / `drop_landed`); Open questions 2 and 3); minor: No test shows the production mapping from Rebase to Rebased: Unchecked becomes Clean with a warning, NeedsRecheck becomes Blocked naming build job 7, and an error after the fetch becomes Blocked. (Decision 5 / Step 8 (`PrLander::rebase` mapping)); minor: Section 6 step 4 says a thrashed job 'closes as an environment-type stop'. The plan only reports it and does not say whether a later wave or drain picks the item up again. (Decision 6 / 8 (thrash)); minor: The work is near the limit of one producer run: a queue, a real rebase, conflict-path extraction, drop_landed, send_back via ask, thrash handling, and about ten new tests across two crates.
